accounts.ask.title: Ask before running a changed harness
accounts.ask.description: wisp keeps the path, size and sha256 of each harness’s program from the first time it runs it. Off, a change shows on the task and here. On, a run on a changed harness waits until you trust it
accounts.tool.gh: For pushing branches and opening pull requests (the gh CLI)
accounts.machine.none: No coding agent that signs in is there yet. Install Claude Code or Codex on it.
accounts.lean.title: Lean Claude Code runs
accounts.lean.description: Without telemetry, error reports and update checks: fewer connections and about a second faster to start. A lean run has no claude.ai connectors (Google Drive, Docs, …), no org memory (Team plans), no /ultrareview or /advisor, no push notifications, and none of Claude Code’s server-rolled features. wisp’s side runs (judges, reviews, the retro) need none of these

accounts.updateAll.title: Updates available
accounts.account.name: Account name
accounts.account.noticeTitle: Only add accounts that are yours.
accounts.account.notice: Each account must belong to you: your own plan, or a seat your employer gave you. Sharing a login with someone else is against Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s terms and can get the account closed.
accounts.account.noticeLimits: Each account keeps its own usage limits. wisp doesn’t combine them, and it won’t switch accounts to get around a limit: when one runs out, it asks you first. Before you use a work account on personal projects, or the other way round, check your employer’s rules.
accounts.account.keepsOwn: The account the CLI signs in with on its own stays; sign it out instead
accounts.account.removeDetail: wisp signs it out and forgets it. Tasks that ran on it keep their history.
